finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: POST /hooks/test sends a POST request to an attacker-supplied URL from req.body.callback with no validation and no auth.

trace.note: pub.post("/hooks/test") route registered on the pub router, which has no auth middleware
req.body.callback passed directly to axios.post with a fixed { ping: true } body
response status code returned to caller, enabling internal host/port probing

finding.guards_checked: None on the path. No auth middleware on pub router (routes.js:4, :19). No type check, scheme restriction, host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local/metadata IP blocking, or redirect restriction (axios follows redirects by default).

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:4 creates the `pub` router with no middleware, and `requireAdmin` (routes.js:7-10) is attached only to `admin` via `admin.use` at routes.js:12, so it does not cover `pub`. routes.js:20 passes `req.body.callback` straight to `axios.post` with no type, scheme, or host check, and axios follows redirects by default. The only other file in the directory is routes.js, so there is no app-level auth or mount point I can see here.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled `req.body.callback` (routes.js:20) reaches `axios.post` on the unauthenticated `pub` router (routes.js:4, :19) with no closing guard, and the status is echoed back at routes.js:21. Caveat: the app file that mounts `pub` is not in this directory, so if it is mounted behind authentication elsewhere the exploitability changes, but the code here has no auth.

finding.claim: Admin-gated SSRF: GET /diagnostics/fetch fetches an arbitrary URL from req.query.url and returns the status code.

trace.note: requireAdmin applied to the whole admin router via admin.use
requireAdmin returns 403 unless req.session.role === "admin"; this is the only guard

finding.guards_checked: Admin session role check only (routes.js:7-9, :12). No URL parsing, scheme or host allowlist, private/loopback/metadata IP blocking, or redirect restriction. Precondition is admin access, so severity is lower than ssrf-1. Unknown whether app-level middleware or an egress proxy exists outside this repo.

verdict.guard_found: No URL validation, scheme/host allowlist, or IP blocking before the sink. The only guard is requireAdmin (routes.js:7-9), applied via admin.use at routes.js:12. That is an authorization check, not a closing URL guard.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:12, 7-9, 14-16), but the source fails: req.query.url at routes.js:15 is only reachable after requireAdmin (routes.js:7-9) passes, so it is admin-controlled, not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker.
